item: A pool timeout on a worker's first checkout is recorded against that source and leaves it for the next pass, instead of ending the whole collect pass
summary: The worker's first pooled checkout is the read of its own Source row, made before _process_source and so outside its handler. With the pool exhausted it timed out (30 s), came out of fut.result() and ended the pass with the remaining sources unscraped. It is now caught there (sqlalchemy TimeoutError only): the failure is logged with the source id, counted as an error in the tally, and the source goes on the existing deferral list (reason pool-timeout) so it runs first next pass; nothing retries within the pass and the other sources carry on. Red without: one source's first checkout raises the pool timeout, at parallelism 2 and 4 (parallelism 1 is the sequential loop, which has no worker); unfixed the pass raises TimeoutError, fixed four store, one is deferred, one error is tallied, the log names the source id. A TimeoutError that comes out of _process_source itself still ends the pass and is recorded with the pass counts (test_run_error_counts unchanged). Reviewed and left: the pass's finally reads s.id on deferred caller-session objects (its ids are loaded, no pooled checkout is needed), and the sequential loop's source.domain read on the caller session (that session already holds its connection).
